prompt: A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. A premium paper-art illustration: the ENTIRE image, edge to edge, is ONE flat sheet of matte deep indigo-navy cardstock (#222B45) with a fine paper grain — no border, no mat, no cream margin, no square plate, no raised panel, nothing but that one indigo sheet around the opening. A round opening shaped like the rim of a big iron cauldron is cut PERFECTLY CENTERED in the sheet, filling about 78 percent of the image width. Looking through the opening you see a deep recessed tunnel of SIX to EIGHT paper layers, each layer cut with the same outline and stepping inward, each casting a soft shadow onto the next; the first two layers are the same indigo paper as the sheet, then the layers shift gradually into the story's colours toward the back. At the back of the tunnel, a small detailed paper-cut scene: an autumn red-bean field and a little thatched cottage under a golden sun, a kind grandmother in hanbok stirring red-bean porridge, and a chubby cute persimmon-orange tiger cub with dark-brown stripes, cream muzzle and pink cheeks peeking over the inner rim with its paws, curls of paper steam. Only a few small story elements may gently overlap the inner rim of the opening; nothing is glued onto the outer indigo sheet. Calm, elegant, harmonious limited palette, soft light from the top left. Cute Korean picture-book characters for 3-4 year olds, never scary. No text.
